questions.question: You're in Manual mode and ask Claude to fix a typo in README.md. What happens?
options: Claude asks before editing the file
Claude edits the file without asking
Claude writes a plan and stops
questions.answer: Claude asks before editing the file
questions.explanation: Manual mode lets Claude read files and run read-only commands freely, but every file edit needs your approval.

questions.question: In Edit automatically mode, Claude has changed three files and now wants to run your tests. What happens?
options: Claude asks before running the tests
Claude runs the tests without asking
Claude runs the tests without asking if they're inside the project
questions.answer: Claude asks before running the tests
questions.explanation: Edit automatically covers file edits and basic file commands such as mkdir and mv inside your project. Running tests is a different kind of shell command, so it still needs your approval wherever the tests live.

questions.question: You want Claude to study a project you've never seen and propose how to restructure it, changing nothing yet. Which mode fits best?
questions.explanation: Plan mode only reads and researches, then writes a plan for you to review. It makes no changes until you approve it.

questions.question: Claude just edited files that you expected it to ask about first. What should you check first?
options: The mode shown under the prompt box
Whether the files are inside your project folder
questions.answer: The mode shown under the prompt box
questions.explanation: A mode that edits without asking, such as Edit automatically or Auto, is probably on. Shift+Tab may have switched it without you noticing, or the session may have started in Auto.

questions.question: Claude is on a long task in Auto mode and starts heading in the wrong direction. What do you do?
options: Wait for its next approval prompt
questions.explanation: Auto mode doesn't stop to ask for approval, so no prompt is coming. You can always press Esc to interrupt.
